Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call follow-up — hands-on workshop?

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the intro call today — the team liked the latency/cost figures you showed. We want to move to a short hands-on workshop where our ML engineers poke at prompt routing and run a few short load tests (non-prod). Can we lock a 90-minute session next week?

Two asks up front so we can prepare:
- Can Redwood provide a short checklist for redaction/PHI so we can scrub the sample prompts?
- What's the recommended sample size for a realistic routing/load run (token distribution, # of unique prompts)?

Availability windows next week (Pacific): Tue 10/13 10:00-12:00, Wed 10/14 14:00-16:00, Fri 10/16 09:00-11:00.

Jordan
Jordan Alvarez
Lead, ML Platform
HelioHealth

--

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call follow-up — hands-on workshop?

Jordan — great to hear. Ben and I can run a 90-minute working session focused on: routing profiles, prompt redaction guidance, and a short load plan to validate batching/kv-cache behavior. Proposed plan:

1) 15m quick recap + goals (who cares: latency vs. cost vs. correctness)
2) 45m hands-on: prompt routing variants + live evals on a small test corpus
3) 20m load run: short bursts (90s) to observe tail latency and throughput
4) 10m next steps + handoff artifacts

We prefer Wed 10/14 14:00-15:30 PT — that fits our specialist availability (Soojin will bring the routing config examples). If that works, please send the sample prompts (we'll provide a redaction checklist).

Attachments attached: redaction_guidance_v1.pdf (two-page checklist), session-load-plan.xlsx (template we use for short runs).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Jordan — quick answers to your asks before we schedule:

- Redaction: aim to remove or mask direct PHI (names, MRNs) and replace with stable pseudo-ids. The attached guidance has a checklist and example sed commands.
- Recommended sample for routing+load: 1,500–5,000 prompts total for routing evaluation (stratified by intent + token length). For the short load bursts we recommend 300–700 unique prompts with a realistic token distribution (we'll provide a sampling script).

Soojin, please add the routing config examples and the sampling script link in your follow-up. Dev, I'll need a quick confirm that the test workspace will have a 2x-CPU quota for the 90s bursts.

If Wed 10/14 14:00 PT works for Helio, we will hold it and send a calendar invite with a shared Drive folder link for uploads.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Marissa / Ben — Wed 10/14 14:00 PT works. We've started redacting and attached a first pass (helio_sample_prompts_redacted.csv). A few quick notes from our side:
- The sample is ~420 prompts (mixed lengths) — does that work for the routing exercise or do you want us to expand the set?
- We redacted names and replaced with user_### pseudo-ids; left timestamps but removed any device IDs.

I've also added a pointer to our internal tokenizer distribution so you can see expected token counts: https://drive.heliohealth.ai/token-dist. We'll upload the full sample set to the Drive folder you share.

Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the upload and the redaction pass, this is perfect for the hands-on. Quick operational notes before the session:

- Please drop the full CSV in this shared folder by EOD Wed 10/07 so we can auto-sample and produce the routing variants. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEF_sample-set
- For the live load bursts we'll convert 300 unique prompts into a burst script (we'll seed repeats to match your expected qps). If you want longer tail coverage, add ~20% more unique prompts.
- Attached: redaction_guidance_v1.pdf (small checklist) and session-load-plan.xlsx (we filled the template with the proposed run: 3 bursts of 90s at 40qps).
